## October 10 Recap: Clean Sheet

You know, in all my years covering this game, there's something deeply satisfying about a perfect day. Nothing fancy, nothing complicated—just one solid pick and one solid result. The Guardians took care of business at home against the Sox, exactly as our model suggested at 53%. Not a dominant probability, mind you, but enough edge to lean Cleveland's way, and they delivered.

## What Worked Yesterday

The Guardians' home-field advantage in October is something I've seen play out time and again. Progressive Field gets loud when the stakes are high, and that 53% edge we identified? It's built on years of data showing how Cleveland performs in these exact situations. Small sample size for the day, sure, but when you nail the call, you take it.

## Looking Ahead: October 11 Preview

Now we get interesting. The Dodgers head to Milwaukee, and if you've been around this game as long as I have, you know this matchup has some serious storylines. Tarik Skubal on the mound for Los Angeles—the guy's been outstanding when healthy. But here's the thing: Jacob Misiorowski gets the ball at home for the Brewers, and our model is leaning Milwaukee at 61%.

## The Brewers Case

Sixty-one percent isn't a slam dunk, but it's a meaningful edge. Milwaukee at home in October, with a capable arm on the mound, against a Dodgers squad that's been traveling—I've seen this script before. The Brewers know how to play tight games, and that home crowd in Milwaukee can be a difference-maker.

Skubal is no slouch, don't get me wrong. But pitching on the road in the postseason is a different animal. The model sees enough here to favor the home side, and frankly, so do I.

## The Bottom Line

We're 1-0 to start this stretch, and tomorrow we're backing the Brewers with solid conviction. October baseball is where reputations are made and broken—I've covered enough of these games to know that the edges matter, even the modest ones.

Let's keep it rolling.

*—Max*
